## Subjective

48yo M, established patient, presents with 3-day h/o intermittent left-sided chest discomfort (location: left chest, retrosternal; quality: pressure-like, non-radiating; severity: 4-6/10; duration: 3 days; timing: with exertion + occasionally at rest; context: stairs at home; modifying factors: improves with rest). Denies SOB, diaphoresis, syncope, nausea. PMH: HTN, hyperlipidemia. FHx: father MI age 52. SHx: ex-smoker 10 pack-years quit 2018. Compliant with lisinopril, atorvastatin.

## Objective

VS: BP 142/86, HR 78, RR 16, T 98.4°F, SpO2 99% on RA. Gen: anxious-appearing, in no acute distress. HEENT: unremarkable. Cardiac: RRR no m/r/g, no JVD. Lungs: CTAB. Abdomen: soft, non-tender. Extremities: no edema, distal pulses 2+. Neuro: A&O×3, no focal deficits.

## Assessment

1. Atypical chest pain, etiology uncertain (R07.9) — differential includes stable angina, GERD, costochondritis. EKG today shows NSR without ST changes. Troponin pending.
2. Hypertension, suboptimally controlled today (I10) — likely related to acute discomfort
3. Hyperlipidemia (E78.5) — on statin

## Plan

EKG performed in office, NSR, no acute ST changes. Troponin sent — will follow up by phone today. Discussed risk stratification: given FHx + age, plan stress test if troponin negative. Started ASA 81mg daily. Continue lisinopril and atorvastatin. Patient counseled to return immediately or call 911 if pain worsens, becomes constant, radiates, or associated with SOB/diaphoresis. F/u in 1 week or sooner pending labs. Office records reviewed; prior cardiology consult from 2024 noted (clean stress test then).
